# site — the official Pergyra homepage, generated by Pergyra

The homepage is built by a **Pergyra program**, `pergyra_home.pgy`. It builds the
page (HTML + CSS + the webtoon-style sequential animation) as text and prints it;
`build.sh` captures that into `dist/index.html`.

This is a dogfood: the same text-emission ability the self-host compiler uses to
emit C, used to emit a website. The mascot **Gyri** (the amber/indigo nautilus)
narrates the page panel by panel, each revealing in sequence.

## Honest scope

Pergyra does **not** run in the browser — there is no WASM/JS backend yet (that
is a future capability). So "written in Pergyra" means the page is *generated by*
a Pergyra program, not *executed* in the browser. The animation it writes is
plain CSS that the browser plays; Pergyra authored it, the browser runs it. When
a WASM backend lands, interactive logic could move into Pergyra too.

## Build

```sh
# from the repo root, with bin/pgy already built
bash site/build.sh
# then open site/dist/index.html
```

`PGY_BIN` overrides the compiler path; `PGY_BACKEND=llvm` switches backend (output
is identical — the page is text).

## Layout

- `pergyra_home.pgy` — the generator (the source of truth for the page).
- `build.sh` — compile + run → `dist/index.html`.
- `dist/index.html` — the generated, deployable page (e.g. for GitHub Pages).

Edit the page by editing the Pergyra generator, never `dist/` directly.
